milestones.title: Architecture is approved and the coding-agent baseline is ready for MCP work
milestones.goal: The mission has an approved architecture and any existing package blockers that would invalidate MCP work are identified and handled first.

verification.expect: The package baseline is green or any remaining blocker is explicitly recorded in mission progress before MCP implementation begins.

verification.command: Review `ARCHITECTURE.md` and `SPEC.md` against the source material from `.factory/library/mcp.md`, `.factory/library/architecture.md`, and `.factory/library/user-testing.md`; confirm the generic-core/Figma-pilot split, transport order, auth stance, and validation order are coherent before implementation begins.
verification.expect: Review confirms the mission boundaries are coherent or reports blocking issues with file references before implementation starts.

verification.command: Run the coding-agent CLI in a temp workspace and inspect the startup/help surface to confirm the package baseline is usable before MCP work begins; capture any visible blocker if startup/help is already degraded.
verification.expect: The visible CLI surface is usable at baseline, or any blocker is explicitly captured as pre-existing evidence.

milestones.notes: Do not begin durable MCP implementation until architecture is approved and the baseline state is understood.

milestones.title: Generic MCP runtime works through the normal Mu runtime surface
milestones.goal: Mu can load MCP config, connect to HTTP-backed servers, discover tools, invoke them through the normal runtime, and recover or refresh without stale state.

verification.expect: Config, auth precedence, and redaction behavior are proven.

verification.command: npm run test -w @kennyfrc/mu-coding-agent -- test/mcp-http-runtime.test.ts test/mcp-http-session.test.ts test/mcp-inventory-refresh.test.ts test/mcp-malformed-data.test.ts test/mcp-tool-naming.test.ts --maxWorkers=4
verification.expect: Discovery, invocation, session continuity, refresh, malformed-data handling, and deterministic naming are proven.

verification.command: Review the generic MCP runtime implementation against `SPEC.md`, focusing on lifecycle ownership, deterministic naming, redaction, recovery, and the rule that remote tools flow through the normal runtime surface.
verification.expect: Review confirms the generic MCP runtime is correctly layered and does not leak Figma-specific behavior, or reports blocking findings with file references.
A deterministic local MCP harness proves connect/discover/invoke behavior through test-only verification without requiring a separate curl contract.
The package remains green with generic MCP runtime changes.

milestones.notes: Figma-specific logic stays out of scope for this milestone.

milestones.title: Figma proves the generic MCP runtime in both deterministic and real validation paths
milestones.goal: The Figma pilot loads through normal runtime paths, shows truthful status UX, and completes at least one meaningful Figma operation through the normal tool pipeline.

verification.expect: The deterministic local MCP harness works on reserved ports and exposes tools end-to-end.

verification.command: npm run test -w @kennyfrc/mu-coding-agent -- test/figma-runtime-loading.test.ts test/figma-tool-exposure.test.ts test/figma-slash-ui.test.ts test/figma-readiness-ui.test.ts test/figma-bearer-auth.test.ts test/figma-oauth-recovery.test.ts test/figma-oauth-capability-gating.test.ts --maxWorkers=4
verification.expect: Figma loading, tool exposure, UX, bearer auth behavior, and login-required capability gating are proven.
Metadata-based OAuth support detection and runtime capability gating are proven against a deterministic harness.

verification.command: Verify Figma slash-command discovery and connection-state UI show disconnected, connecting, connected, and degraded/auth-failed states truthfully.
verification.expect: Visible UX matches actual callable runtime state.

verification.command: Review the Figma pilot implementation against `SPEC.md`, focusing on pilot-layer boundaries, truthful readiness UX, auth recovery behavior, metadata-driven OAuth support detection, and evidence that the normal tool pipeline is used end-to-end.
verification.expect: Review confirms the Figma pilot is layered correctly on the generic runtime, surfaces truthful status, and gates OAuth-backed capability exposure from metadata rather than guesswork, or reports blocking findings with file references.

verification.command: Run one real Figma validation path against the configured endpoint and capture concrete Figma-specific output, or record an explicit external blocker.
verification.expect: Real validation either succeeds meaningfully or is blocked only by missing external access/credentials.
The repo remains green after MCP and Figma pilot work.

milestones.notes: This milestone is not complete until the visible UI and actual tool surface agree.
